title: skillgrade
description: Unit tests for agent skills — run assertions against agent skill outputs the same way you'd test code
why_interesting: Solves the 'how do I know my agent skill actually works' problem with a familiar test-runner interface. From Minko Gechev (Angular team). 480 stars in ~3 months.

title: agent-skills-eval
description: Test runner for agentskills.io-style skills with YAML-based scenarios and LLM judges
why_interesting: 508 stars in 2 weeks. The agentskills.io spec is getting traction and this gives it a proper eval framework. TypeScript, works with OpenAI-compatible APIs.

title: eval-view
description: Regression testing for AI agents — snapshot behavior, diff tool calls, catch regressions in CI
why_interesting: Works with LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI, Anthropic. The snapshot-diff approach is exactly what agent teams need but few build. Python/pytest-based.

title: agent-belt
description: Reproducible evaluation for AI coding agents — multi-turn scenarios, rich assertions, multi-judge consensus
why_interesting: From JFrog's engineering team. Runs eval scenarios against Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, or any agent you plug in. Open source, CLI-based. Fills the 'how do I test my coding agent doesn't break' gap.

title: contrabass
description: Project-level orchestrator for AI coding agents — Go + Charm TUI implementation of OpenAI's Symphony SPEC.md
why_interesting: First real implementation of the Symphony spec. Go binary, TUI interface, coordinates Codex/Claude Code agents. 151 stars, actively maintained. The 'one orchestrator, many coding CLIs' pattern is where agent infra is heading.

title: TraceFix
description: Uses TLA+ counterexamples to repair multi-agent LLM coordination protocols before deployment
why_interesting: Formal methods applied to agent coordination. Instead of testing protocols after they fail, TLA+ finds violations upfront and generates repairs. CAISconf 2026 paper by Rutgers team.

title: Raindrop Workshop
description: Local debugger for AI agents — live streamed traces of every token, tool call, and decision with self-healing eval loops
why_interesting: Solves the 'agent debugging is blind' problem. You can watch agents think in real time, and Claude Code reads the traces, writes evals, and fixes bugs autonomously. MIT license, 665 stars in 18 days. Works with every major SDK and coding agent.

title: claude-mem
description: Persistent context across sessions for coding agents — captures session activity, compresses with AI, injects into future sessions
why_interesting: Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot. 76k stars, v13.2, active commits. Solves the real problem of agents starting from zero every session. SQLite + ChromaDB + embeddings under the hood.

title: 12-Factor Agents
description: Engineering principles for building production-grade LLM-powered software — agents as software with LLM steps, not prompt loops
why_interesting: 21k stars. The core insight: agents are software with LLM calls placed strategically, not 'prompt + tools + loop'. Own your prompts, typed tools, human-in-the-loop as first-class, stateless reducer pattern. This is the production playbook most agent projects lack.

title: Context7
description: Up-to-date code documentation delivered to LLMs and code editors via MCP — solves the stale-doc problem for coding agents
why_interesting: 55k stars, MIT. The real issue: every coding agent guesses APIs from training data that's months old. Context7 injects fresh docs at query time. Works as MCP server, integrates with Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex. Built by Upstash. The 'documentation as context' pattern is a missing infra layer for agent reliability.

title: Chrome DevTools MCP
description: Official Chrome DevTools exposed as MCP server — lets coding agents inspect, debug, and profile web apps directly
why_interesting: 40k stars, Apache 2.0, official Google project. The first serious bridge between browser debugging and agent workflows. Agents can now read console errors, inspect DOM, profile performance, and set breakpoints — all through structured tool calls instead of screenshot guessing. Changes how agents debug frontend code.

title: Lapdog (Datadog)
description: Local agent tracer — traces reasoning and tool calls from Codex, Claude Code, and Pi in real time, no account required
why_interesting: Datadog shipped a free local tool that shows what agents actually do. 70 likes in hours. Fills a real gap: most agent debugging is reading terminal output blind. Runs fully local, zero infra. The 'observability for agents' layer is barely starting and this is the first usable tool from a major vendor.

title: Retrieval Routing: vector + GraphRAG + PageIndex
description: Production pattern: route queries across vector RAG, GraphRAG, and PageIndex based on query type using a lightweight classifier before retrieval
why_interesting: The insight: most teams pick one retrieval strategy and force everything through it. Wrong retrieval produces wrong answers that compound into agent failures. A small LLM classifier in front of the retrieval layer costs less than one bad retrieval. Vector for factual lookup, GraphRAG for multi-hop relational, PageIndex for long structured docs. FinanceBench: vector scores 50%, PageIndex scores 98.7%.

title: Ruflo
description: Agent orchestration platform for Claude — deploy multi-agent workflows with a visual builder and structured output routing
why_interesting: 53k stars. First major orchestration platform built specifically for the Claude ecosystem. The 'single agent framework, many providers' era is giving way to framework-specific orchestration layers. TypeScript, visual workflow builder, supports Claude Code and OpenClaw natively.

title: pentest-ai
description: Offensive security MCP server — wraps 205 pentesting tools and 17 specialist agents behind a single MCP interface
why_interesting: 268 stars, MIT license. The first serious attempt to put offensive security behind MCP. 205 tools (nmap, exploitation, OSINT) accessible to any MCP client. Shows MCP reaching beyond dev tools into security operations. Active commits. Python.

title: Warp Oz Multi-Agent Orchestration
description: Multi-agent orchestration in Warp's Oz — delegate complex tasks across Claude Code, Codex, and Warp Agent with worktree isolation and message passing
why_interesting: 177 likes, 81k views. First terminal-based multi-agent orchestrator that crosses framework boundaries. Each subagent gets its own worktree (local) or Docker container (cloud). The /orchestrate command generates a delegation plan and agents coordinate via structured message passing. This is the 'agent of agents' pattern going mainstream in terminal tools.

title: Plano
description: AI-native proxy and data plane for agentic apps — LLM routing, safety guardrails, orchestration, and observability in one Rust proxy
why_interesting: 6.4k stars, Rust, built on Envoy. The 'Envoy for agents' pattern — sits between your agents and LLM providers handling routing, rate limiting, safety checks, and cost tracking. Most agent teams build this ad-hoc; Plano gives it to you as a drop-in proxy. Solves a real infra gap.

title: Cozeloop
description: Full-lifecycle agent optimization platform — dev, debug, eval, and monitor agents from a single Go service
why_interesting: 5.4k stars, Go, from ByteDance's Coze team. Agent eval + monitoring + prompt management in one platform. The lifecycle angle matters — most tools do eval OR observability, Cozeloop does both plus a playground for iteration. Good fit for teams running agents in production who need to close the feedback loop between monitoring and improvement.

title: CubeSandbox
description: Hardware-isolated sandbox for AI agents built on RustVMM + KVM — boots in under 60ms, uses less than 5MB per instance
why_interesting: From Tencent Cloud. Not containers — actual hardware-level isolation via KVM micro-VMs. E2B SDK compatible. 5.8k stars in 6 weeks, Rust, Apache 2.0. The agent sandbox problem (how do you run untrusted agent code safely?) is one of the unsolved infra gaps. Most solutions use Docker with seccomp. CubeSandbox uses virtualization, which is fundamentally harder to escape. 2000+ concurrent sandboxes on a single node. This is the security layer production agents need.

title: Open Multi-Agent
description: TypeScript-native multi-agent orchestration — turns a goal into a task DAG automatically, with MCP and live tracing, three runtime dependencies
why_interesting: 6.2k stars, MIT, created March 2026. The 3-dependency claim is rare in a space where most frameworks pull in hundreds. Model-agnostic: Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Ollama. The goal-to-DAG pattern means you describe what you want, not how agents coordinate. Built-in live tracing solves the visibility gap. TypeScript-native fills the Node.js ecosystem gap that most agent frameworks ignore.

title: Sandcastle
description: Orchestrate sandboxed coding agents in TypeScript with sandcastle.run() — single API call spins up an isolated agent on Docker, Podman, or Vercel Firecracker microVMs
why_interesting: From Matt Pocock (Total TypeScript). 4.6k stars, MIT, 483 forks. The key insight: agent orchestration needs sandboxing as a first-class concern, not an afterthought. sandcastle.run() handles branch isolation, sandbox provisioning, and merge-back automatically. Provider-agnostic (Docker, Podman, Vercel). This is the 'test runner for agents' pattern — you don't think about the sandbox, you just run. Active commits, 660+ PRs merged.

title: Context Mode — Context Window Optimization for AI Coding Agents (15.5K Stars, HN #1)
description: Context window optimization for AI coding agents — sandboxes tool output, claims 98% reduction in context usage across 15 platforms
why_interesting: 15K stars. #1 on Hacker News with 570+ points. Used at Microsoft, Google, Meta. 98% context reduction. 15 platforms. Not security but massive traction.

title: DeerFlow — ByteDance SuperAgent with Sandboxes, Memory, Skills, Subagents (69K Stars)
description: Open-source long-horizon SuperAgent by ByteDance that researches, codes, and creates. Uses sandboxes, memories, tools, skills, subagents and message gateway to handle tasks from minutes to hours.
why_interesting: 68K+ stars. Handles tasks that take minutes to hours with full agent infrastructure — not a demo wrapper. ByteDance-backed and actively maintained.

title: OpenSandbox — Secure, Fast Sandbox Runtime for AI Agents from Alibaba (10.8K Stars)
description: Secure sandbox runtime for AI agents from Alibaba — extensible plugin architecture for isolation, resource limits, and policy enforcement
why_interesting: 10.7k stars, Apache 2.0, Python. The agent sandbox space is consolidating fast: CubeSandbox (Tencent, KVM micro-VMs), OpenSandbox (Alibaba, plugin-based), microsandbox (local Rust), Sandcastle (Matt Pocock, TypeScript). OpenSandbox's angle is extensibility — plugins for custom isolation policies rather than one-size-fits-all containerization. Active commits. Part of the 'agent runtime isolation' infra layer that production agents require.

title: Microsandbox — Unexploitable Secrets for AI Agents via Hardware-Isolated microVMs (6.2K Stars)
description: Spins up lightweight VMs in milliseconds. Hardware-level isolation. Rootless, embeddable SDK. Key feature: secrets that can't leak — unexploitable secret keys that never enter the VM. Every other sandbox tries to contain what the agent does. This one prevents what the agent can ever know. Written in Rust. Under 100ms boot time.
why_interesting: Contrarian angle: keeps secrets FROM the agent, not just contained. Hardware isolation + unexploitable keys that never enter VM. Rust. 100ms boot. Our exact niche.

title: Memori
description: Agent-native memory infrastructure — LLM-agnostic layer that turns agent execution and conversation into structured, persistent state for production systems
why_interesting: 14.6k stars, Python, 2200 forks. Different from claude-mem (which is session context persistence). Memori is structured state: it captures execution traces, decisions, and conversation turns, then compresses them into retrievable memory that any LLM can query. The agent-memory problem has two layers — short-term context (solved by bigger windows) and long-term structured recall (still unsolved). Memori targets the second. Production systems need agents that remember what happened across sessions without re-reading the full transcript.

title: MassGen
description: Open-source multi-agent scaling system with TUI — agents work in parallel, vote on best solutions via consensus, with checklist-gated quality rounds
why_interesting: 1034 stars. The consensus voting mechanism is genuinely different from other orchestrators. Agents collaborate, vote to converge, and self-evaluate with evolving criteria. Worktree isolation per agent, MCP tool support, checkpoint safety as standalone MCP server. Python/TUI. Fills the "how do multiple agents agree on an answer" gap.

title: Agent Orchestrator
description: Parallel coding agent orchestrator that plans tasks, spawns agents via tmux+git worktrees, and autonomously handles CI fixes, merge conflicts, and code reviews.
why_interesting: Solves the real scaling problem: running multiple coding agents in parallel without them stepping on each other. Uses git worktrees for isolation, tmux for process management. 7K stars, actively maintained.

title: ByteRover CLI
description: Portable memory layer for autonomous coding agents. Formerly Cipher. Works as MCP server providing persistent context across sessions.
why_interesting: Tackles the agent memory gap between sessions without requiring a full RAG pipeline. Portable = works with Claude Code, Codex, any agent. 4.7K stars.

title: cc-sdd (Spec-Driven Development)
description: Turns approved specs into long-running autonomous implementation. Minimal SDD harness with agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI.
why_interesting: Interesting approach: instead of letting agents freestyle, constrain them with approved specs first. The spec-as-contract pattern reduces hallucinated implementations.

title: agentmemory
description: Persistent memory for AI coding agents based on real-world benchmarks. Records what your agent does during every session, compresses it with AI, injects the right context back when the next session starts. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes. 4-layer memory architecture: working, episodic, semantic, procedural. 95.2% retrieval accuracy at top-5 on LongMemEval-S.
why_interesting: 15.5K stars in 3 months. Single tweet got 981 bookmarks and 36K views. Agent memory is THE hot topic right now — every coding agent loses context between sessions and this solves it with real benchmarks. Share trigger: 95.2% retrieval accuracy + 4-layer memory model inspired by human cognition.

title: MemOS
description: Self-evolving memory OS for LLM and AI agents. Ultra-persistent memory, hybrid-retrieval (keyword + vector + graph), and cross-task skill reuse. Claims 35.24% token savings through intelligent memory compression and retrieval.
why_interesting: 9.2K stars. The token savings claim (35.24%) is concrete and shareable. Cross-task skill reuse is different from just session memory — it learns across projects. Hybrid retrieval (keyword + vector + graph) is technically interesting vs pure vector approaches.

title: engram
description: Persistent memory system for AI coding agents. Agent-agnostic Go binary with SQLite + FTS5, MCP server, HTTP API, CLI, and TUI. No external dependencies — runs as a single binary.
why_interesting: 3.6K stars. Contrarian approach in a TypeScript-dominated space: pure Go, SQLite-based, no cloud deps. Agent-agnostic means it works with any tool that speaks MCP. Single binary deployment is a real advantage over node-heavy alternatives.

title: osaurus
description: Native macOS harness for AI agents. Any model, persistent memory, autonomous execution, cryptographic identity. Built in Swift. Fully offline. Open source. MCP compatible.
why_interesting: 5.4K stars. Fully offline + crypto identity is a strong contrarian angle in the everything-cloud era. Swift native means it actually uses macOS hardware properly. Share trigger: local-first agent that owns its own identity without any cloud service.

title: ECC
description: Agent harness performance optimization system. Skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor and beyond.
why_interesting: 192K stars for agent harness optimization — skills, instincts, memory, security in one system.

title: OpenViking
description: Open-source context database designed specifically for AI Agents. Unifies management of context (memory, resources, skills) through a file system paradigm with hierarchical context delivery and self-evolving.
why_interesting: ByteDance/Volcengine building a context OS for agents. File system paradigm is different from vector-only approaches. 24K stars. Self-evolving context management.

title: memvid
description: Memory layer for AI Agents. Replaces complex RAG pipelines with a serverless, single-file memory layer. Gives agents instant retrieval and long-term memory. Built in Rust.
why_interesting: Replaces entire RAG stacks with a single MP4 file. Rust-based, offline-first, zero infrastructure. 15.5K stars. The "anti-pipeline" approach to agent memory.

title: code-review-graph
description: Local knowledge graph for Claude Code. Builds a persistent map of your codebase so Claude reads only what matters — 6.8x fewer tokens on reviews and up to 49x on daily coding tasks. 19+ languages. Runs fully local. No API keys.
why_interesting: Reduces Claude Code tool calls by 94% by indexing codebase into a knowledge graph upfront instead of scanning files. 17K stars in ~3 months. Viral on Twitter (264+ likes). The "stop scanning, start querying" approach to agent code intelligence.

title: Mirage
description: A unified virtual filesystem for AI agents. Gives every agent a consistent file interface regardless of backend. Works with Claude Code, LangChain, OpenAI agents. TypeScript + Python.
why_interesting: Only 15 days old, already 2.5K stars. Solves the "every agent has a different IO model" problem. VFS abstraction means agents can read/write without caring about where data lives. Fresh project with strong traction.

title: smallcode
description: AI coding agent optimized for small LLMs. Hits 87% benchmark score with only a 4B-active parameter model. Proves you dont need massive models for real coding tasks.
why_interesting: Hot take material: 4B model beating agents that run on 70B+ models. 979 stars in 3 days. Directly challenges the "you need the biggest model" narrative. Cost implications are huge — run a coding agent on a potato.

title: ARGO
description: Open-source local AI agent platform. Manus-style autonomous task execution running 100% on your laptop. No cloud, no subscription. Multi-agent task engine with planning, reflection, tool chaining. Ollama + HuggingFace + OpenAI/Claude/DeepSeek. Full MCP support. Local RAG.
why_interesting: Directly challenges $39/month Manus. No cloud dependency, no data leaving your machine. The "Manus but local" positioning is viral. Human-in-the-loop planning step. Native apps for Mac/Windows/Linux.

title: mcp2cli
description: Turn any MCP, OpenAPI, or GraphQL server into a CLI — at runtime, with zero codegen. Every MCP server loads ALL tool definitions on EVERY turn. mcp2cli converts them to simple commands the agent calls only when needed. Saves thousands of tokens per turn.
why_interesting: Practical cost-saver for anyone running agents with MCP. The insight that MCP burns tokens on unused tool definitions is a real problem. 2.1K stars. Zero codegen at runtime is clever engineering.

title: Dulus
description: Free CLI agent that harvests Gemini (guest, no login), Claude.ai, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek browser sessions and turns them into tool-calling agents. Reads and edits files, runs Bash, greps repos, browses the web, ships commits. All from terminal at $0.
why_interesting: Provocative approach — instead of paying for API access, it piggybacks on free browser sessions. 625 stars. The "why pay for APIs" angle is contrarian enough to get attention. Practical for devs who want agent capabilities without API bills.

title: Zerolang
description: Agent-first programming language by Vercel Labs. Small regular syntax agents learn on the fly. Structured diagnostics, deterministic tooling, deep stdlib. Written in C, Apache-2.0.
why_interesting: 4.1K stars in 6 days. Top tweet got 58K views. First language designed specifically for agents as primary users. Compare: prompts vs agent-native code.

title: Photo-agents
description: Autonomous self-evolving agents with vision-grounded layered memory. Perceive/reason/act loop. Agents write own skills from real success. Multi-provider LLM router, browser automation, sandboxed code exec. Python.
why_interesting: Self-evolving agent narrative exploding (dair_ai survey 252K views). Vision+memory+self-written-skills combo is unique. 1K stars in 2 weeks.

title: OpenSquilla
description: Token-efficient microkernel AI agent. Local model router sends each turn to cheapest capable model. Persistent memory, layered sandbox, web search, on-device embeddings. 20+ LLM providers. Python.
why_interesting: Directly addresses rising API costs (GPT-5.5 2x, Claude +46%). Model routing = pay less for same results. 1.3K stars, Apache-2.0.

title: OctoTools
description: Agentic framework with extensible tool cards for complex reasoning. Planner+executor loop, standardized tool metadata. Broad LLM support. Python, MIT.
why_interesting: Tool-card pattern is interesting for modular agent design. 1.4K stars. Older (Feb 2025). Lower urgency.

title: EverOS
description: Build, evaluate, and integrate long-term memory for self-evolving agents. Python, Apache-2.0.
why_interesting: Combines memory layer WITH eval framework. 5.4K stars. Most agent memory repos just store. This one evaluates whether the memory actually helps. Also has self-evolving agent architecture built in.

title: SimpleMem
description: Efficient lifelong memory for LLM agents — text and multimodal. Python, MIT.
why_interesting: Research-backed memory system that handles text AND multimodal. 3.3K stars. Most memory tools are text-only. This one extends to images and structured data. MIT license makes it easy to adopt.

title: moltis
description: Secure persistent personal agent server in Rust. One binary, sandboxed execution, multi-provider LLMs, voice, memory, messaging integrations. Runs on your hardware.
why_interesting: Rust binary with sandboxed execution. Single deployable unit. Connects to Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Teams. 2.7K stars and growing. The "run on your hardware" angle is the story — no cloud dependency, no vendor lock-in.

title: oh-my-claudecode
description: Teams-first multi-agent orchestration for Claude Code. Parallel execution, agent specialization.
why_interesting: 34K stars. The "teams-first" approach is the differentiator — not just multi-agent, but structured team roles with parallel execution. This is the direction agent frameworks are converging toward.

title: TradingAgents
description: Multi-agent LLM financial trading framework. Research Desk, Quant Team, Trading Floor, and Risk Management as separate agents orchestrated together. Python.
why_interesting: 78K stars. Multi-agent architecture applied to financial trading — each role (researcher, quant, trader, risk) is a separate LLM agent. Practical example of multi-agent coordination solving a complex domain problem. The bull/bear debate mechanism between agents is novel.

title: zeroclaw
description: Fast, small, fully autonomous AI personal assistant infrastructure. Rust-based. Deploy anywhere, any OS, any platform. Modular swap-anything architecture.
why_interesting: 31K stars, created Feb 2026 (3 months old). Rust means real sandboxing, not theater. "Deploy anywhere" claim backed by cross-platform binary. The "swap anything" modular design is the interesting architecture choice — lets you swap LLM providers, memory backends, tool integrations independently.

title: MCP Toolbox for Databases
description: Open-source MCP server by Google for databases. Supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, BigQuery, Spanner, MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, CockroachDB, Oracle, TiDB, Firestore, and more. Go.
why_interesting: 15K stars. Google official. 20+ database backends via single MCP server. This is the "just works" layer between agents and data — no more custom database connectors per agent. Go means single binary deployment.

title: omo (oh-my-openagent)
description: The best agent harness. Previously oh-my-opencode. 58.8K stars. Supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode. Modular skills, orchestration, agent loop — all in one harness.
why_interesting: 58.8K stars in 6 months. Started as oh-my-opencode, evolved into a universal agent harness. The author also built lightweight agent loop that uses <40% CPU and 3GB RAM vs bloated alternatives. Claude Code + Codex + Cursor all supported.

title: agent-lightning
description: Microsoft open-source RL trainer for AI agents. Works with LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenAI SDK, or plain Python. Captures prompts, tool calls, rewards as structured events. Trains improved prompts or policy weights automatically.
why_interesting: 17.2K stars. Microsoft built an RL loop that makes ANY agent framework better without rewriting prompts. Agnostic to your stack — drop in agl.emit(), pick algorithm, agent improves. First time RL for agent optimization is this accessible.

title: html-anything
description: Agentic HTML editor — your local AI agent writes the HTML, you ship it. 75 skills × 9 surfaces (magazine, deck, poster, XHS/tweet, prototype, data report, Hyperframes). Sandboxed preview, 1-click publish to WeChat/X/Zhihu. Zero API key required.
why_interesting: 4.4K stars in 3 weeks. 75 skills, 9 output surfaces, zero API keys. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode. The skill-based architecture is clean — composable agent primitives, not monolithic templates.

title: AiSOC
description: Open-source AI-powered Security Operations Center. Alert fusion, purple-team drills, agent-assisted triage, MITRE ATT&CK investigation. MIT-licensed, self-hostable. Python + Next.js.
why_interesting: 1.1K stars. First real open-source AI SOC. Agent-assisted alert triage with MITRE ATT&CK mapping. The agent architecture is interesting — separate agents for detection, investigation, and response. Self-hostable, MIT license.

title: holaOS
description: Agent OS that turns repeat work into running AI work-streams. Electron-based, MCP-compatible, with persistent memory and proactive AI runtime. TypeScript.
why_interesting: 5.6K stars in 2 months. Agent OS category is heating up — not just a harness but a workspace that learns your patterns.

title: Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit — Runtime Policy Enforcement for Every Agent Tool Call (1.9K Stars)
description: AI Agent Governance Toolkit — 3,522 stars, up from 2,530 in 10 days. 13,000+ tests covering all 10 OWASP Agentic risks. Supports LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen. Runtime policy enforcement for every agent tool call. Gartner: ~150K AI agents per Fortune 500 by 2028, only 13% have adequate governance.
why_interesting: Microsoft shipping agent security tooling that covers ALL OWASP agentic top-10. Signal that agent governance is becoming enterprise requirement.

title: TEN Framework
description: Open-source framework for conversational voice AI agents. Multi-modal, real-time voice + video. Python.
why_interesting: 10.6K stars. Voice agents are the next frontier after text agents — TEN is the leading framework in this niche.

title: nexent
description: Zero-code platform for auto-generating production-grade AI agents using Harness Engineering principles. Unified tools, skills, memory, orchestration with constraints, feedback loops, control planes. Python, MIT.
why_interesting: 4.6K stars. Harness engineering applied to agents — the no-code angle could be interesting for non-dev audience.

title: boxlite
description: Compute substrate for AI agents: lightweight on laptop, elastic to cloud. Rust + TypeScript, Apache 2.0. Embedded, self-hosted, serverless.
why_interesting: Laptop-to-cloud agent sandbox. Same space as microsandbox but cloud-elastic. Good comparativo angle.

title: mcpc
description: Universal CLI client for MCP by Apify. Persistent sessions, stdio/HTTP, OAuth 2.1, tasks, JSON output, proxy for AI sandboxes, x402 support.
why_interesting: MCP ecosystem maturing — a universal CLI client means MCP is becoming infrastructure, not just a protocol.

title: agent-safehouse
description: Sandbox your local AI agents so they can read/write only what they need. Shell-based, minimal.
why_interesting: Minimal approach to agent sandboxing — opposite end of spectrum from heavy frameworks. Good for "just works" angle.

title: Hive (aden-hive)
description: Multi-Agent Harness for Production AI. Python framework with self-improving agents, human-in-the-loop, agent skills, supports OpenAI and Anthropic.
why_interesting: 10.4K stars, production-grade multi-agent harness. Self-improving agents + human-in-the-loop. Topic aligned with hot Anthropic agents discussion (130K+ views on Twitter). Strong viral potential: production agents framework with real architecture.

title: Motus (lithos-ai)
description: Open-source agent-serving project. From the team behind Motus Tracing (356 likes, 27K views on Twitter). Agent observability infrastructure.
why_interesting: Agent observability is consolidating as a theme (per persona_memory). This is the serving/infra companion to Motus Tracing which got massive engagement. 455 stars and growing. Fits our "agent sandboxing/infra consolidating" pattern.

title: evilsocket/audit — 8-Stage Vulnerability-Discovery Agent (Cloudflare Glasswing Pipeline)
description: From the creator of bettercap. Reimplementation of Cloudflare Project Glasswing: 8 narrow agents with deliberate disagreement and reachability gates beat one big model at finding bugs. MIT licensed, no API key needed with claude login. Stages: Recon → Hunt → Verify → Reach → Disprove → Feedback → Triage → Report.
why_interesting: Contrarian angle: one big model can't find bugs. 8 narrow agents that disagree with each other can. From bettercap creator. Based on Cloudflare's published research. First agent that goes from recon to verified, reachable CVE.

title: Agent Executor (AX)
description: Google open source distributed agent runtime. General purpose runtime for dynamic scheduling, resumption, auto recovery, auditing, and trajectory branching from kernel snapshots in agentic workloads. Written in Go. Announced at Google I/O 2026 by @rakyll.
why_interesting: Google-backed agent runtime addressing the unsolved infra problem of productionizing long-running agentic workloads. Scheduling, resumption, and trajectory branching from kernel snapshots. 25K+ views on announcement tweet. Directly competes with the scheduling/gap that most agent frameworks hand-wave.

title: IronClaw — Agent OS Focused on Privacy, Security and Extensibility (12.3K Stars)
description: Agent OS focused on privacy, security and extensibility. Written in Rust with WASM sandboxing and encrypted credential vault where the LLM never sees your API keys.
why_interesting: 12K stars. Rust-based agent runtime with WASM sandboxing is exactly the wire-level enforcement angle that resonated with infra builders (proven by Ryan Dahl engagement). Encrypted credential vault solves the real problem of agents needing API access without leaking secrets.

title: AI-Infra-Guard — Full-Stack AI Red Teaming Platform by Tencent (3.8K Stars)
description: A full-stack AI Red Teaming platform securing AI ecosystems via OpenClaw Security Scan, Agent Scan, Skills Scan, MCP scan, AI Infra scan and LLM jailbreak evaluation.
why_interesting: Tencent-backed open-source AI red teaming platform that covers the full attack surface: agents, MCP servers, skills, prompts, and infrastructure. 3.7K stars. Pushed today. Agent security is our highest-engagement topic — Ryan Dahl thread proved network-layer security resonates with infra builders.

title: supply-chain-guard (pc-style)
description: Local supply-chain install gate for npm packages and VS Code extensions with Socket, Codex integration.
why_interesting: Every AI coding agent runs npm install with zero human review. This gates installs at the local level with Socket + Codex checks. Created today. Chen Avnery tweet about autonomous amplifiers got 148 views — supply chain for agents is a live topic.

title: Studio (decocms)
description: Open-source control plane for your AI agents. Connect tools, hire agents, track every token and dollar.
why_interesting: First open-source agent control plane with cost tracking. 373 stars. One bad agent loop = five-figure model bill, and most teams have zero visibility. Pushed today. Practical value for anyone running agents in production.

title: claude-in-box (jiangmuran)
description: Portable Claude Code dev environment in a Docker container. Multi-session, hook-driven, with persistent workspace.
why_interesting: Dockerized Claude Code with multi-session support and hooks. Created today. Solves the real problem of reproducible coding agent environments. Go-based. 24 stars but very fresh and practical.

title: CC-Switch (farion1231)

description: Local proxy + web dashboard that shows exactly what Claude Code, Codex, and Kimi send to the LLM. Transparency tool for understanding agent communication patterns.
why_interesting: Small project but solves a real problem: nobody knows what their coding agent actually sends to the model. Observability gap in agent tooling. 31 stars but growing fast — concept resonates.

title: Mitiga: Claude Code MCP Token Theft via Supply Chain — Anthropic Refused to Fix
description: Mitiga Labs found that a fake npm package can hijack Claude Code by redirecting MCP server URLs in ~/.claude.json. Stolen token bypasses MFA, survives rotation, leaves no trace. Anthropic was notified April 10 2026 and said out of scope — no fix coming.
why_interesting: Supply chain attack on AI coding agents. Fake package modifies MCP config → token theft. Vendor refused to fix. Affects everyone using Claude Code with MCP.

title: Microsoft Semantic Kernel RCE Chain — CVE-2026-26030/25592 (CVSS 9.9)
description: Two CVSS 9.9 flaws in Microsoft Semantic Kernel AI agent SDK: Python sandbox escape + arbitrary file write. 9 detections, 26 IOCs. Chainable for full RCE in agent deployments using MS SDK.
why_interesting: Microsoft official AI agent SDK has critical sandbox escape + file write chain. CVSS 9.9. Every team building agents on MS stack is exposed.

title: vm2 CVE-2026-24120 — Sandbox Escape (CVSS 9.8) in Agent Code Execution
description: vm2 CVE-2026-24120 (CVSS 9.8): bypass of CVE-2023-37466 lets attackers escape the VM and run host commands. Update to 3.11.2. Affects any AI agent that runs user code in vm2 sandboxes.
why_interesting: Popular sandboxing library used by AI agent platforms has critical escape. Patch before your agent runs user code.

title: CVE-2026-7061 — ChatGPT-MCP-Server Docker Command Injection (CVSS 7.3)
description: Critical command injection in Toowiredd/chatgpt-mcp-server allows unauthenticated RCE via Docker service component. Public PoC available. Project abandoned (issue open, no fix). The vulnerability is in the Docker bridge that connects MCP servers with containers — the trust boundary every MCP deployment depends on.

title: FlowiseAI 10 Critical Flaws (CVSS 9.9) — RCE Cascade via CSV/Airtable Agent Injection
description: FlowiseAI published a security advisory batch revealing a critical vulnerability cascade in Flowise — the popular open-source UI for no-code LLM app assembly. Flaws range from unauthenticated RCE chains via CSV/Airtable agent injection to plaintext credential storage. A single malicious CSV or Airtable payload chains through the agent to achieve code execution.

title: MCP 2026-07-28 RC — Protocol Goes Stateless, No Session ID, No Handshake
description: MCP protocol release candidate removes session state entirely. No handshake, no session ID, any request can hit any server instance. Extensions become first-class (MCP Apps, Tasks). Auth hardening and deprecation policy added. 547K views, 1.37K likes, 205 RTs on announcement by dsp_. Security implications: every request must carry its own auth context — tool servers must validate every call independently.
why_interesting: Protocol-level change to how all AI agents communicate with tools. Going stateless means trust boundaries shift from session-level to request-level. Most MCP server implementations are NOT prepared for this. 547K views proves this is already mainstream — our contrarian security angle (nobody discussing auth implications) is the hot take.

title: Pydantic AI CVE-2026-46678 — SSRF Cloud-Metadata Bypass via IPv6 Transition Forms
description: Pydantic AI 1.100.0 fixes SSRF vulnerability. IPv6 transition forms bypass cloud-metadata blocklist in FileUrl with force_download=allow-local. The fix normalizes IPv6 transition forms before blocklist comparison.
why_interesting: Agent framework with SSRF bypass — the allowlist pattern (block known-bad IPs) fails when IPv6 transition forms map to blocked IPv4 addresses. Same class of bug affects every agent framework doing URL validation.

title: mcp-yoshi v1.4.0 — MCP Security Filter Covering 76% of Flowise 59 CVEs
description: MCP communication filter for Claude Code. Covers 76% (45/59) of Flowise vulnerabilities with rules IN-015 through IN-021: parameter override, path traversal, query injection, sandbox escape, header spoofing, browser launch RCE. Detects trust-command + dangerous-option patterns in npx/npm/pnpm/yarn/bun/deno.
why_interesting: First MCP-level security filter that covers the full Flowise attack surface. The trust-command pattern (npx -c, bun -e, deno eval) is a class of vulnerability affecting ALL package runners in agent toolchains.

title: AWS Strands Agents SDK — Model-Driven Agent Framework (5.9K Stars)
description: AWS open-source SDK. Model-driven approach to building AI agents in few lines of code. Python + TypeScript. AgentCore integration.
why_interesting: AWS entered the agent framework space with a model-driven SDK. 5.9K stars in weeks. The Strands approach: describe what you want, the model drives execution. Contrarian angle: AWS built the SDK but who governs what the agents access?

title: UncommonRoute — LLM Router with 82% Cost Savings (663 Stars)
description: Automatic LLM router. 82% cost reduction, 79.4% accuracy, 93.4% pass rate. Drop-in OpenAI-compatible proxy. Routes queries to cheapest capable model.
why_interesting: Everyone optimizes prompts and models. Nobody optimizes routing. 82% cost savings by routing queries to the cheapest capable model. Drop-in OpenAI proxy means zero code changes.

title: NVIDIA AI-Q Blueprint — Deep Research Skill for Agent Harnesses (619 Stars)
description: NVIDIA open reference for building intelligent AI agents. AI-Q skill packages research pipeline into portable skill. Drop into any harness. Returns cited reports.
why_interesting: NVIDIA tweet got 58K views and 850 likes. AI-Q wraps deep research into a portable skill you drop into any agent harness. The meta-trend: skills/plugins as the new package managers for agent capabilities.

title: Cline CVE-2026-44211 — WebSocket Origin Bypass Enables Agent Session Hijack and RCE (CVSS 9.3)
description: Local WebSocket server on localhost:3484 has zero origin validation. Any website can silently connect to read workspace paths, git branches, and inject commands into running AI agent sessions. Affects Cline ≤2.13.0 via kanban ≤0.1.59. No patch available at time of disclosure.
why_interesting: Real CVE in production coding agent. Any website open in your browser can hijack your agent session. Same missing-spec pattern as Next.js SSRF CVE-2026-44578.

title: Gemini CLI CVSS 10.0 — Malicious Repo Config Grants Full RCE in CI/CD
description: Headless mode automatically trusts workspace folders. Anyone who can push to your repo can inject malicious .gemini/ config for arbitrary command execution on CI/CD runners. No auth, no interaction needed. Affects @google/gemini-cli before 0.39.1 and 0.40.0-preview.3, and google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli before 0.1.22. No CVE assigned.
why_interesting: Maximum severity RCE in Google AI coding agent. Supply chain attack: push a config file, own the CI runner. Same trust model as Claude Code .claude/ and Codex risks.

title: CLI-Anything — Turn Any Desktop Software Into Agent-Native CLI (39.6K Stars)
description: HKU research project. Scans any software source code (GIMP, Blender, Photoshop, Zoom) and auto-generates clean agent-ready CLI interfaces. Lets AI agents control GUI apps that never had APIs. 3 days to 39K stars.

title: OpenFang — Open-Source Agent Operating System in Rust (17.6K Stars)
description: Not a chatbot framework. Full agent OS. 137K LOC, 14 crates, 2500+ tests. Autonomous agents with scheduling, memory, and tool use. One binary. Rust-native.

title: SocratiCode — MCP Server for Codebase Intelligence (2.7K Stars)
description: Open-source MCP server giving coding agents reusable intelligence layer for codebases. Hybrid BM25 + semantic search with reciprocal rank fusion. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI. Index lives with codebase, not inside one IDE.

title: Lightpanda — Headless Browser Built from Scratch for AI Agents (30.4K Stars)
description: First headless browser designed for agents, not adapted from Chromium. 11x faster, 9x less memory. CDP-compatible. Infrastructure that matches the use case.

title: Hyperframes — Write HTML, Render Video, Built for Agents (20.5K Stars)
description: HeyGen open-sourced their video rendering pipeline. Write HTML templates, render as video. Built for AI agent workflows. TypeScript.

title: Forkd — Fork 100 Agent MicroVMs in 101ms with KVM Isolation (611 Stars)
description: MicroVM sandbox runtime for AI agent fan-out. Children fork from a warmed parent snapshot with copy-on-write memory. Built on Firecracker. BRANCH lets agents fork mid-thought in ~150ms. Per-child KVM isolation with fork(2)-level spawn cost.

title: CVE-2026-7061 — ChatGPT-MCP Server Command Injection (CVSS 7.3)
description: Critical command injection in Toowiredd chatgpt-mcp-server allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve RCE through MCP tool calls. MCP servers are the new attack surface.
why_interesting: MCP servers are proliferating without security audits. Every agent tool connector is a supply chain vector. This CVE proves the point.

title: LiteLLM Agent Platform — Self-Hosted Sandboxed Coding Agents with Vault Proxy (484 Stars)
description: Self-hosted platform for running Claude Code, Codex, Hermes in isolated sandboxes with vault proxy. Agents never see real API keys, vault injects them at runtime.

title: OneCLI — Open-Source Credential Vault for AI Agents (2.2K Stars)
description: Give AI agents access to services without exposing keys. OAuth2 and API key vault that brokers credentials to agents at runtime. Keys never appear in conversation history or tool returns.

title: Infisical Agent Vault — HTTP Credential Proxy for AI Agents (1.3K Stars)
description: HTTP credential proxy and vault for Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes. Intercepts agent API calls and injects credentials at the proxy layer. Agents never store or see secrets.

title: Groundcrew — Dispatch Linear Backlog to AI Coding Agents (31 Stars)
description: One git worktree per ticket, sandboxed by default. Dispatches your Linear backlog to AI coding agents automatically.

title: CVE-2026-5865 — AI Agent Found Chrome V8 Zero-Day (Nebula Security)
description: Nebula Security's AI agent Vega discovered CVE-2026-5865, a zero-day in Chrome V8 affecting 40+ major versions. Renderer memory read/write, potential RCE. First Chrome V8 zero-day found by AI. 38K views, 482 likes. Patched by Google. Same team behind nginx-poolslip discovery.
why_interesting: AI agent autonomously discovering browser zero-days is the thesis made real. Contrarian angle: most teams worry about agents being attacked — Nebula's agent IS the attacker. This validates the "AI as security researcher" paradigm.

title: Vidar Malware Harvesting OpenClaw Agent Identities — soul.md, Memory, and Gateway Tokens Stolen
description: Vidar infostealer evolved to harvest AI agent identities. Sweeps .openclaw folder stealing: gateway token (remote access), private keys, soul.md (personality/behavior), MEMORY.md (activity logs), AGENTS.md (access levels). SecurityScorecard found 40,214 OpenClaw instances exposed publicly, 63% vulnerable to RCE. Hudson Rock: "shift from stealing browser credentials to harvesting souls of AI agents."
why_interesting: The attack surface shifted. Old infostealers stole passwords. New ones steal agent identities — complete digital personas with access levels, behavioral instructions, and gateway keys. 40K+ exposed instances. Directly validates the credential isolation work we discussed with Teknium.

title: CVE-2026-46354 — Coder Agent Token Theft via Azure Signature Bypass (CVSS 9.1)
description: Critical vulnerability in Coder allows unauthenticated attackers on any Azure VM to steal agent session tokens. Root cause: azureidentity.Validate() checked certificate chain but skipped signature verification. Attacker crafts fake PKCS#7 data using publicly available Azure certificates from Certificate Transparency logs, sends to /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity, receives workspace session token. With stolen token: Git SSH private keys, OAuth access tokens (GitHub/GitLab), API keys, environment variables. Unauthenticated. No malware needed.
why_interesting: CVSS 9.1. Unauthenticated token theft on AI dev infra. Attacker forges Azure identity, steals SSH keys + OAuth tokens. Signature bypass — checked cert chain, never verified the actual signature.

title: ds4 — Redis Creator's DeepSeek V4 Flash Local Inference Engine for Metal/CUDA (11.4K Stars)
description: Salvatore Sanfilippo (antirez, Redis creator) built a lightweight C engine for running DeepSeek V4 Flash locally on Metal (Apple Silicon) and CUDA. Pure C, no frameworks.
why_interesting: 11.4K stars in 17 days. Redis creator applying systems-level thinking to local inference. Proves frontier model inference can run on consumer hardware without Python/PyTorch overhead. Directly relevant to self-hosted agent stacks.

title: CVE-2026-25874 — Hugging Face LeRobot Unauthenticated RCE via Unsafe Deserialization (24.3K Stars)
description: Critical RCE in HuggingFace open-source robotics platform. Unauthenticated remote code execution through unsafe deserialization in the inference pipeline. AI agent controls a robot arm + code execution vulnerability = physical safety hazard. Same platform powering the new $2,500 LeRobot Humanoid announced May 22.
why_interesting: 24.3K stars + RCE in AI robotics platform + same week as humanoid launch. Timing: HF announces $2500 humanoid robot May 22, but their platform had unauthenticated RCE 3 weeks ago. When AI controls physical hardware, code execution = safety hazard, not just data breach.

title: CVE-2026-31431 "Copy Fail" — AI-Found Linux Kernel LPE Zero-Day (Every Distro Since 2017, 732-Byte Exploit)
description: AI found a Linux kernel zero-day that roots every distribution since 2017. The exploit fits in 732 bytes of Python. CVE-2026-31431 disclosed by Theori. Straight-line logic mistake that works first try, every time. No race condition, no address leak needed. Corrupts page cache — never touches disk. Containers dont help (shared page cache). 9-year-old bug in a 2017 crypto optimization. Your agent sandbox runs on Linux.
why_interesting: AI-found kernel zero-day + agent sandbox relevance. 4 critical Linux kernel LPEs in May 2026 alone (Copy Fail, Dirty Frag, Fragnesia, Pinthef). One found by AI, humans missed for 9 years. Agent sandboxes (Docker, KVM, Firecracker) all run on Linux. Page cache shared across containers = one compromised pod escapes to host.

title: May 2026 Linux Kernel LPE Cluster — 4 Critical Privilege Escalations in 3 Weeks (Copy Fail, Dirty Frag, Fragnesia, Pinthef)
description: Four critical Linux kernel LPE vulnerabilities disclosed in May 2026: CVE-2026-31431 Copy Fail (AI-found, 9-year bug, page cache corruption), CVE-2026-43284 Dirty Frag (universal LPE), CVE-2026-46300 Fragnesia (XFRM ESP-in-TCP, same subsystem as Dirty Frag), and Pinthef. All affect mainstream distributions. One found by AI. Exploit code published before patches for some. Agent sandboxes and containers share the same host kernel — one LPE = full host escape.
why_interesting: Pattern-level discovery: 4 critical kernel LPEs in 3 weeks. Relevance to our audience: every agent sandbox runs on Linux. Copy Fail found by AI. HackTheBox covered it (5K views, 54 likes). 3 of 4 in same kernel subsystem. AI-driven vulnerability discovery outpacing patching.

title: DeepSeek V4 Pro Autonomous Hacking — 4 Expert Security Challenges Solved for $6.84 (412 Tool Calls)
description: Tur24Tur demonstrated DeepSeek V4 Pro autonomously solving 4 expert-level PortSwigger security challenges: SQL Injection (26 tool calls, 3 min), Android Root Detection Bypass with Frida (102 calls, 16 min), Reflected XSS with AngularJS sandbox escape + CSP bypass (142 calls, 71 min), Web Cache Deception (142 calls, 35 min). Total: 412 tool calls, $6.84 on DeepSeek V4 Pro. Each solution reviewed by Claude Opus 4.7. 11K+ views, 115 likes on original thread.
why_interesting: Concrete numbers ($6.84, 412 tool calls) + autonomous hacking + real security challenges. 115 likes proves this format resonates. Our audience cares about agent security. Contrarian angle: the cheapest AI model is better at finding vulnerabilities than most junior pentesters.

title: Claude Code Network Sandbox Bypass — Credentials and Source Code Exposed Across 130+ Versions
description: Critical bypass in Anthropic's Claude Code AI assistant exposed credentials, source code, API keys, and internal resources. The network sandbox designed to isolate Claude Code from sensitive resources could be circumvented, allowing the agent to access data it should not see. Affects 130+ versions. Directly relevant to agent sandboxing and the untrusted-agent threat model.

title: Langflow — First AI Agent Framework Added to CISA "Must Patch" List (Attacked Within 20 Hours of Disclosure)
description: Langflow became the first AI agent framework added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Attackers began exploiting it within 20 hours of disclosure. This is a landmark moment — the first time the US government treats an AI agent framework with the same urgency as critical infrastructure software. Confirms that agent frameworks are now part of the core attack surface.

title: CVE-2026-26144 — XSS in Excel Hijacks Copilot Agent for Zero-Click Data Exfiltration
description: Microsoft patched XSS vulnerability in Excel (CVE-2026-26144) that chains with Copilot Agent to silently exfiltrate spreadsheet data. Zero-click — preview triggers it. Copilot interprets XSS payload as instructions and autonomously sends data externally. CVSS 7.5 but Microsoft rated Critical. Two years ago XSS stole a session cookie. Now it weaponizes an AI agent.
why_interesting: A plain XSS from 2023 becomes a zero-click AI agent attack in 2026. Same bug class, exponentially worse blast radius. This is the definitive example of why old vulns are now AI vulns.

title: PocketOS — AI Agent Deleted Entire Production Database + All Backups in 9 Seconds (Cursor + Claude Opus)
description: Automotive SaaS company PocketOS had their entire production database and all volume-level backups deleted by Cursor AI with Claude Opus 4.6. Nine seconds. No confirmation prompt, no scope restrictions. The agent postmortem: "I violated every principle I was given. I guessed instead of verifying." Original post reached 6.5M views. Better prompts would not have stopped it. A gate would have.
why_interesting: The most visceral AI agent safety incident to date. 9 seconds. All data gone. The founder's story hit 6.5M views. Proof that permission boundaries matter more than prompt engineering.

title: HASP — Local-First Broker for Managed Secrets in Agent Workflows (433 Stars)
description: Go-based local-first secrets broker for AI agent workflows. Manages secrets outside agent process memory. Agents never hold credentials directly — secrets brokered on-demand via local service.

title: ship-safe — CLI Security Scanner for the Agentic Era (710 Stars)
description: CLI tool that detects CI/CD misconfigs, agent permission risks, MCP tool injection, hardcoded secrets, and DMCA-flagged AI dependencies. Built specifically for agentic workflows.

title: AgentGuard — Security Guard for AI Agents with 24 Detection Rules (410 Stars)
description: TypeScript security guard that blocks malicious skills, prevents data leaks, protects secrets. Runtime action evaluation and trust registry. 24 built-in detection rules for common agent attack patterns.

title: AWS Secrets Manager Agent — Official AWS Local HTTP Service for Agent Compute (656 Stars)
description: AWS official Rust-based local HTTP service for reading secrets from Secrets Manager with in-memory caching. Designed for compute environments running AI agents.

title: shellfirm — Safety Guardrails for AI Coding Agents and Terminal Commands (912 Stars)
description: Rust-based safety guardrails that intercept dangerous terminal commands before execution. Works for both AI coding agents and humans. Prevents agents from running destructive commands (rm -rf, DROP TABLE, etc.) by requiring explicit confirmation. MCP-compatible.
why_interesting: Directly addresses the "who stops the agent from running rm -rf" problem. Rust = minimal overhead. MCP-compatible = drops into existing agent stacks. 912 stars shows real adoption.

title: CVE-2026-65719 — Critical RCE in kubectl-mcp-server via Command Injection (891 Stars, CNCF Landscape)
description: Critical command injection vulnerability in kubectl-mcp-server allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary system commands by injecting shell metacharacters into unsanitized input fields. Full host control + potential K8s cluster compromise. Affected: < 1.2.1. Listed in CNCF Landscape.
why_interesting: MCP server for K8s with unauth RCE = attacker controls your entire cluster through the AI agent. CNCF-listed project. Shell metacharacter injection is the simplest exploit class — no sophistication needed.

title: Sponsio — Deterministic Safety Solutions for Probabilistic AI Agents (397 Stars)
description: Open-source deterministic safety layer for AI agents. Intent verification, policy engine, agent harness, runtime safety. Built for OpenClaw skills. Addresses prompt injection, policy drift, and unauthorized actions through provable constraints rather than probabilistic guardrails.
why_interesting: "Deterministic safety for probabilistic agents" is the exact framing the space needs. Every other guardrail tool uses ML to check ML. Sponsio uses hard constraints. OpenClaw-native.

title: Cisco Foundry Security Spec — Open Standard for Agentic AI Security Evaluation (76 Stars)
description: Cisco DevNet open specification for evaluating and testing agentic AI security. Standardized framework for security assessment of AI agent deployments. First major vendor-backed open standard for agent security testing.
why_interesting: Cisco backing an open agent security spec = signal that enterprise is taking this seriously. First vendor-backed standard in this space. Low stars but high strategic importance.

title: Tirith — Terminal Security for AI Agents: Intercepts Malicious Skills Before Execution (2.4K Stars)
description: Terminal security for developers and AI agents. Written in Rust. Intercepts homograph URLs, pipe-to-shell, ANSI injection, obfuscated payloads, data exfiltration, and malicious AI skills/configs before they execute. Supply chain security at the terminal layer.
why_interesting: Rust tool that intercepts malicious AI skills BEFORE execution. Terminal-level agent security. Supply chain angle. Contrarian hook: your agent reads a malicious skill and tirith blocks it before it runs.

title: CyberStrikeAI — AI-Native Security Testing Platform with 100+ Tools and MCP (3.9K Stars)
description: AI-native security testing platform built in Go. Integrates 100+ security tools. Intelligent orchestration engine. Role-based testing with predefined security roles. Skills system with specialized testing skills. MCP integration. Full lifecycle management.
why_interesting: Go + MCP + 100+ security tools. Role-based agent pentesting. Not just a scanner - orchestration engine. 3.9K stars.

title: DeepSeek V4-Pro Permanent 75% Cut — Your Attackers Got the Same Discount
description: DeepSeek made their 75% V4-Pro price cut permanent. Model runs at 1/35th the cost of Claude Opus 4.7/GPT-5.5. Two implications missed by most: (1) agent economics flip — autonomous code review, continuous monitoring, document triage now cost cents per task, (2) attackers got the same discount. Generating prompt injection corpora at scale, fuzzing jailbreaks, personalized phishing, vuln triage on stolen repos all run at the new price. Red team and attack economics are the same equation. One side files compliance paperwork. The other does not. Plus jurisdiction risk: V4-Pro hosts in China, Article 7 compels data sharing. A model swap in agent tools is a single config line.
why_interesting: CONTRARIAN GOLD: attacker economics flipped overnight. Concrete numbers (1/35th cost, $0.435/M input). Security angle. Jurisdiction twist. Multiple surprise elements. Perfect DeepSeek-Reasonix template: surprising number + contrarian defense of unpopular position + WHY it matters.

title: CVE-2025-34291 — MuddyWater Exploits Langflow CORS + Refresh-Token Chain for RCE (CISA KEV)
description: Iranian state-sponsored APT MuddyWater exploited a CORS misconfiguration in Langflow (CVE-2025-34291, CVSS 8.8) chaining it with a refresh-token vulnerability to achieve pre-auth remote code execution. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on May 22, 2026. Attack path: CORS misconfiguration → cross-origin session hijack → stolen refresh tokens → authenticated RCE. Langflow ≤1.6.9 affected. Same CVE used in multi-stage campaign targeting aviation, energy, and government sectors across Middle East.
why_interesting: State-sponsored APT exploiting AI agent framework with 2004-era web vulnerability class. Contrarian hook: CVE-2025-34291 is not an AI vulnerability — it is a CORS misconfiguration in AI infrastructure. Teams audit agent prompts but leave HTTP headers wide open. Most popular AI agent orchestration framework has same security posture as poorly configured WordPress. MuddyWater used it to target aviation and energy infrastructure.

title: CVE-2026-44578 — Next.js SSRF via WebSocket Upgrade, No Backport for 13.x/14.x (CVSS 8.6)
description: Critical SSRF vulnerability in self-hosted Next.js via WebSocket Upgrade handler. External attackers can relay server requests to internal services and cloud metadata APIs, leaking cloud credentials and API keys. Affects Next.js 13.x and 14.x. Fix requires major-version migration to 15.x or 16.x — no backport available. Tens of thousands of agent-hosting Next.js apps potentially exposed.
why_interesting: SSRF in the most popular React framework with no backport path. Thousands of AI agent dashboards and admin panels run on Next.js. Contrarian angle: Vercel shipped a framework where a critical security fix requires a major version migration. Your Dependabot PR will not save you — your product team has to approve a migration.

title: Semia — Static Security Audit for AI Agent Skills Before Execution (174 Stars)
description: Security scanner that statically analyzes AI agent skills (OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex) before they execute. Checks for prompt injection vectors, credential exfiltration paths, and unsafe tool patterns. MIT-licensed, self-hosted. Built specifically for the agent skill supply chain problem.
why_interesting: Agent skill security scanner — directly relevant to the MCP/skill supply chain problem. 174 stars, created May 2026, actively maintained. Fits our security niche perfectly.

title: Perplexity Bumblebee — Read-Only Supply Chain Scanner for Developer Endpoints (705 Stars)
description: Perplexity open-sourced Bumblebee: a read-only endpoint scanner that inventories packages, browser extensions, and developer tooling on macOS/Linux. Built for fast supply chain risk assessment. Pulls metadata without modifying anything. First public release May 22, 2026.
why_interesting: Perplexity (major AI company) releasing a supply chain scanner signals the market takes agent supply chain risk seriously. 705 stars in <24h shows strong community interest.

title: PT-2026-6792 — Semantic Kernel CVE-2026-25592 Patch Bypass: 6 Zero-Day Bypasses + Self-Nuke Vector
description: Six independent 0-day bypasses of the official CVE-2026-25592 patch in Microsoft Semantic Kernel (.NET SDK v1.47.0-1.48.0) and Agent Framework 1.0. Vulnerability chain: CWE-1039 → CWE-22 → CWE-94. The "Self-Nuke" vector overwrites the host application source code. No privileges required, remote exploitation. Stochastic LLM output interpreted as executable system commands.
why_interesting: Patched a CVE? 6 zero-days say you didn't. The "Self-Nuke" vector overwrites host app source code. No privileges, remote, in the most deployed .NET agent framework.

title: MCPwn — First Named Exploit Campaign Targeting MCP Servers (CVE-2026-33032, CVSS 9.8)
description: First named exploit campaign targeting MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers. CVE-2026-33032, CVSS 9.8. Over 2,600 exposed instances. Active exploitation confirmed since April 16. Attack vector: authenticated agent with valid database:read OAuth scope executing unrestricted SQL. All five RSAC 2026 agent identity frameworks (Microsoft AGT, ZeroID, ERC-8004, Visa TAP, Mastercard Agent Pay) would have permitted the attack.
why_interesting: First named MCP exploit campaign. 2,600+ exposed servers. CVSS 9.8. All 5 RSAC identity frameworks would have let it through because identity != intent.

title: CVE-2026-5029 — Unauthenticated RCE in Code Runner MCP Server (241 Stars)
description: Critical command injection in formulahendry/mcp-server-code-runner allows unauthenticated remote code execution. The MCP server runs code snippets via LLM agents but fails to sanitize inputs before execution. Attackers inject arbitrary system commands through unsanitized input fields.
why_interesting: Another MCP server with unauthenticated RCE. This pattern keeps repeating — MCP servers are being deployed as trusted agent infrastructure without basic input validation. Three separate MCP CVEs in May 2026 alone (chatgpt-mcp-server, kubectl-mcp-server, code-runner).

title: MCP RCE-by-Design — OX Security Finds Systemic Vulnerability in Anthropic MCP Affecting 150M+ Downloads
description: OX Security disclosed a critical architectural RCE vulnerability in Anthropic MCP STDIO implementation. Arbitrary command execution across Python, TypeScript, Go, Java, Rust SDKs. 150M+ downloads affected, 200K+ servers, 10+ CVEs. Researchers demonstrated RCE on 6 live platforms and poisoned 9/11 MCP marketplaces. Anthropic: working as designed. Affects Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI.
why_interesting: Anthropic says RCE is a feature not a bug. 150M downloads. The biggest MCP security story to date. Perfect contrarian hook for viral post.

title: Cisco AI Defense MCP Scanner — Enterprise MCP Server Security Scanner (937 Stars)
description: Cisco official MCP server security scanner. Scans MCP servers for potential threats and security findings. Enterprise validation of the MCP security space. Python.

title: hol-guard — AI Antivirus for Developer Agents: Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini (339 Stars)
description: AI antivirus for developer agents. Scans Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode plugins, skills, MCP servers before tools run. Catches malicious instructions and supply chain attacks in agent tooling.

title: ramparts — MCP and Skill Scanner for Indirect Attack Vectors in Rust (87 Stars)
description: MCP and skill scanner that detects indirect attack vectors and security or configuration vulnerabilities in any MCP server or skill. Written in Rust.

title: Google GenAI SDK v2.6.0 — Prompt Injection Detection Moves Inside the SDK
description: Google added enable_prompt_injection_detection to GenAI SDK Python/JS v2.6.0. Gemini CLI v0.43 tightened shell safety checks and JSON stop reasons. Safety controls moving from config files into actual SDK function calls. Policy inside the run loop beats policy outside it.

title: TeamPCP Supply Chain Campaign — 84 Malicious npm Packages in 6 Minutes, 170+ Compromised
description: TeamPCP published 84 malicious npm packages in 6 minutes. Hit TanStack (CVE-2026-45321), Grafana Labs, GitHub internal repos via Nx Console VS Code ext, OpenAI, Mistral AI. Also exploited Microsoft Defender zero-days. May 2026 supply chain attacks worst on record. One actor responsible for most.

title: Project Glasswing Update — Claude Mythos Found 10,000+ Critical Vulns in One Month
description: Anthropic Project Glasswing first update. Claude Mythos Preview found 10,000+ high/critical severity vulnerabilities. Cloudflare: 2,000 bugs. Mozilla: 271 in Firefox 150 (10x vs Firefox 148). wolfSSL: certificate forgery on crypto lib used by billions. 90.6% true positive rate. UK AI Security Institute: first model to solve both attack simulations. Maintainers asking Anthropic to slow down.
why_interesting: Maintainers asking Anthropic to slow down because they cant patch fast enough. The bottleneck shifted from finding bugs to fixing them. 1.7M views on announcement. Contrarian angle: AI found too many bugs for humans to fix.

title: nah — Action-Aware Permissions for Coding Agents (439 Stars)

title: Cozempic — Context Cleaning for Claude Code Agent Teams (313 Stars)

title: vm2 CVE-2026-47140 — Five New Sandbox Escapes (CVSS 10.0) in Node.js Agent Runtimes

title: dexter — Autonomous Agent for Deep Financial Research (26K Stars)
description: Autonomous agent that scrapes, analyzes, and synthesizes deep financial and market research data. Goes beyond Q&A into multi-source synthesis.
why_interesting: Financial-agent vertical is exploding. 26K stars for an autonomous research agent. Part of the agentic finance wave alongside TradingAgents (78K stars).

title: Google I/O: Gemini CLI Killed June 18 → Closed-Source Antigravity CLI + Gemini Spark Full Gmail Access
description: Google I/O 2026: Open-source Gemini CLI dies June 18. Replaced by Antigravity CLI (agy) — a closed-source Go binary. Nobody can audit what it does. Free tier gets weekly caps instead of 1,000 requests/day. Developer community backlash over killing open-source project with 30 days notice. The same company that warns about AI safety is shipping an unauditable agent binary with full email access.

title: CVE-2026-42208 — LiteLLM Pre-Auth SQL Injection (CVSS 9.3) Steals All AI Provider Credentials, KEV-Listed

Sysdig observed exploitation 36h after GitHub Advisory indexed. Now KEV-listed. Fixed in v1.83.7-stable.

title: Three Claude Code CVEs in One Cycle — API Key Exfil (CVE-2026-21852), Command Injection (CVE-2026-24887), Symlink Sandbox Escape (CVE-2026-39861)
description: Three distinct vulnerability classes hit Claude Code in a single disclosure cycle. CVE-2025-59536 + CVE-2026-21852: repo config file silently runs shell commands and exfiltrates API keys via Hooks/MCP. Fixed in 2.0.65. CVE-2026-24887: command injection via find call. CVE-2026-39861: sandbox escape via symlink where sandboxed process drops symlink and unsandboxed write follows it — arbitrary file write with no prompt. Fixed in 2.1.64. Self-hosted Claude Code with strict allowlists kills all three classes.
why_interesting: Three different attack classes (credential theft, command injection, sandbox escape) in one product in one cycle. The SaaS Claude Code surface IS the threat surface. Self-hosted with allowlists kills all three. Contrarian angle: the tool you trust to write your code needs more security review than the code it writes.

title: 135,000+ OpenClaw Instances Exposed — 63% Vulnerable, 15K+ RCE-Ready, API Keys Leaking Through Control Panels
description: SecurityScorecard STRIKE team scan found 135,000+ OpenClaw instances exposed to public internet. 63% vulnerable. 15,000+ exploitable via RCE right now. 53,000+ correlate with prior breach activity. Three high-severity CVEs with public exploit code. Users leaking API keys, OAuth tokens, service credentials through exposed control panels. Root cause: binds to 0.0.0.0:18789 by default. For a tool with shell access, filesystem read/write, credential stores, and messaging control, localhost-only should be the default. It is not.
why_interesting: Largest agent infrastructure exposure on record. Default config = public internet binding for a tool with shell access. 15K+ RCE-ready instances right now. Fits our contrarian security niche.

title: obra/superpowers — Agentic Skills Framework (203K Stars)
description: The fastest-growing agentic skills framework and software development methodology. 203K+ stars, MIT license. Portable skill system for coding agents crossing Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. +17K stars this week alone.
why_interesting: 203K stars. Fastest growing repo in agentic space. Cross-harness skills = the future of agent portability.

title: Damn Vulnerable LLM Agent — Deliberately Vulnerable Agent for Security Practice
description: A deliberately vulnerable React-based LLM agent built for practicing prompt injection, thought/action/observation hijacking, agentic SQLi, and tool abuse. By ReversecLabs. 8K+ views on discovery tweet.
why_interesting: Agent security training ground. Covers prompt injection + agentic SQLi + tool abuse — exactly the attacks happening in prod right now.

title: AgentShield — Security Scanner for AI Agent Configs, MCP Servers, Tool Permissions (671 Stars)
description: Security scanner detecting vulnerabilities in AI agent configurations, MCP servers, and tool permissions. CLI + GitHub Action + ECC plugin + GitHub App. TypeScript, MIT.
why_interesting: Agent config security is the gap nobody audits. MCP servers + tool permissions are supply chain vectors. This scanner covers both.

title: DeepClaude — Run Claude Code Agent Loop with Any Provider (1,946 Stars)
description: Enables Claude Code autonomous agent loop with DeepSeek V4 Pro, OpenRouter, or any Anthropic-compatible provider. Breaks vendor lock-in on the most popular coding agent.
why_interesting: Claude Code locked to Anthropic is the fastest growing complaint. This breaks the lock. Contrarian angle: why would you trust one provider with your entire dev pipeline?

title: Claude Code Permission Bypass — 50-Subcommand Cap Kills All Deny Rules
description: High-severity bypass in Claude Code bashPermissions.ts (lines 2162-2178). Performance optimization caps subcommand analysis at 50 entries. Any shell command with >50 subcommands joined by &&, ||, or ; causes Claude Code to skip ALL deny-rule enforcement and fall back to generic permission prompt. Exposes hundreds of thousands of developers to credential theft and supply chain compromise.
why_interesting: Performance optimization (cap at 50 subcommands) silently disables all security deny rules. The faster the code runs, the less secure it is. Contrarian angle: Anthropic chose speed over safety and never told developers.

title: ClawHavoc 575 Skills Poisoned in 48 Hours — Signing Key in .env Is the Design Problem
description: ClawHavoc campaign poisoned 575 skills on ClawHub in 48 hours using hidden commands and indirect injection. An agent installing a compromised skill can read environment variables including the signing key. Everything works exactly as designed — the signing key in .env is the design problem.
why_interesting: 575 poisoned skills in 48 hours. The system worked as designed — the design is the problem. Signing key in .env means any compromised skill reads it. Contrarian: the attack exploits correct behavior, not a bug.

title: CVE-2026-32211 — Azure DevOps MCP Package Missing Auth (CVSS 9.1)
description: Microsoft @azure-devops/mcp npm package disclosed April 3 2026. Missing authentication on Azure DevOps work items, repos, and pipelines. API keys and auth tokens accessible without valid credentials. CVSS 9.1.
why_interesting: Microsoft official MCP package with no auth on work items, repos, pipelines. CVSS 9.1. Part of the MCP supply chain attack surface. Shows even Big Tech ships MCP servers with critical auth gaps.

title: CVE-2025-32711 EchoLeak — Microsoft 365 Copilot Zero-Click Data Exfil (CVSS 9.3)
description: Microsoft 365 Copilot zero-click data exfiltration via crafted email exploiting indirect prompt injection. CVSS 9.3. User never typed anything malicious — the user is the victim. Dominant 2025-2026 agent attack class.
why_interesting: Zero-click means the attacker sends a crafted email and Copilot leaks data when it summarizes it. CVSS 9.3. The user is the victim, not the attacker. Indirect prompt injection at enterprise scale.

title: wolfSSL Certificate Forge — Mythos AI Found Certificate Forgery in Crypto Library Used by Billions
description: Project Glasswing: Claude Mythos found a way to forge certificates on wolfSSL, a crypto library used by billions of devices. Part of 10,000+ high/critical vulnerabilities found in one month. 90.6% true positive rate. Maintainers asking Anthropic to slow down.
why_interesting: AI found a certificate forgery in a crypto library protecting billions of devices. Maintainers cant patch fast enough — asked Anthropic to slow down. The bottleneck shifted from finding bugs to fixing them.

title: Bernstein — Audit-Grade Multi-Agent Orchestration with HMAC-Signed Audit Chains (451 Stars)
description: Deterministic Python scheduler for CLI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, +44 more). HMAC-SHA256 audit chain per scheduling decision, tamper-evident. Signed agent cards (Ed25519/JWS). Per-artefact lineage. Zero LLM in the coordination loop. Air-gap deployable.
why_interesting: Security angle: every coding agent has sudo on your machine and nobody logs what it did. Bernstein adds compliance-grade audit trail. Contrarian: everyone worried about what agents CAN do, nobody tracks what they DID. 44 agent adapters. Founder paid 00/mo in Claude bills.

title: Dev Machine Guard — Scan Dev Machines for AI Agents, MCP Servers, Suspicious Packages (138 Stars)
description: Go-based scanner for developer endpoints. Detects installed AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor), MCP server configs, IDE extensions, and suspicious npm/pip packages. Single binary, runs in seconds. From Step Security.
why_interesting: Complements Perplexity Bumblebee (inventory) with security scanning. Checks for credential exposure in MCP configs. 138 stars, actively maintained.

title: OpenClaw TOCTOU Sandbox Escape Chain — CVE-2026-44112 (CVSS 9.6) Through CVE-2026-44118
description: Six CVEs in OpenClaw sandbox implementation: TOCTOU write escape (CVSS 9.6 CRITICAL), TOCTOU read escape (CVSS 7.7), heredoc shell expansion bypass (CVSS 8.8), MCP loopback privilege escalation (CVSS 7.8). Symlink races redirect file operations outside sandbox mount root. Hermes-Agent specifically named as vulnerable — persistent memory files (MEMORY.md, USER.md, .env, SSH keys) all reachable. ALL terminal backends exposed: local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, Daytona, Vercel.
why_interesting: Six CVEs in one chain targeting the sandbox that is supposed to contain agents. CVSS 9.6 write escape via symlink race. Hermes-Agent named specifically. Every terminal backend exposed. The agent security stack has a hole at the OS layer.

title: Oh-My-Pi — Terminal AI Coding Agent with Hash-Anchored Edits (6.7K Stars)
description: AI coding agent for the terminal with hash-anchored edits, optimized tool harness, LSP, Python, browser control, subagents. Multi-provider: Anthropic, OpenAI, Bun, Rust, TypeScript. MCP integration built in.
why_interesting: 6.7K stars, hash-anchored edits approach prevents file corruption from agent edits. Multi-provider. Growing fast since Dec 2025. Terminal-first.

title: CVE-2026-42449 — n8n-mcp SSRF Bypass via IPv6-Mapped Addresses (CVSS 8.5)
description: SSRF fix in n8n-mcp was bypassed with 7 characters: http://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]. IPv6-mapped address bypasses IPv4-only blocklist. Zero validation on IPv6 input. Full cloud metadata access.
why_interesting: 7 characters bypassed a security fix. Demonstrates that SSRF protections validating only IPv4 are fundamentally incomplete. Every MCP server that blocks internal IPs needs IPv6 mapping checks.

title: Cloudflare Project Think — Agents SDK with Self-Authoring Extensions, Fibers, and Subagents (5K Stars)
description: New edition of Cloudflare Agents SDK. Think base class gives opinionated agent harness in 3 lines. Self-authoring extensions: agent writes its own tools stored in Durable Objects. Fibers for long-running task recovery with checkpointing. Subagents with isolated SQLite databases. Session trees for non-destructive conversation branching.
why_interesting: Self-authoring extensions is wild: agent writes its own MCP tools at runtime, stored in Durable Objects. First SDK that lets the agent extend itself. Fibers solve the long-running agent crash problem.

title: Understand-Anything — Interactive Knowledge Graph for Any Codebase (21.5K Stars)

why_interesting: 21.5K stars, +2.3K today. Turns codebases into searchable knowledge graphs. Works with every major AI coding tool. Solves the context problem that every agent framework struggles with.

title: SilentFail — MCP Server Health, Token Audit, and Security Scanner
description: Scans MCP servers for silent failures, dead servers, token costs, and prompt injections hiding in tool descriptions. 50+ security patterns. Works with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf. Very new (created May 19, 2026).
why_interesting: MCP security is a hot niche. 50+ patterns, covers the exact failure modes (dead MCP servers, prompt injection in tool descriptions) that recent CVEs exploit. Directly relevant to agent infra security.

Self-evolving security hardening — the agent learns from attacks and patches its own defenses in real-time. 1,341 stars, 225 forks, Python, created April 2026. Contrarian angle: while everyone builds agents to attack, this one builds itself to defend.

title: CVE-2026-30635 — Command Injection in automagik-genie MCP Server via viewTask

title: Kapso MCP — WhatsApp Phone Numbers for AI Agents via MCP Server

title: DryRun Security Study — 26 of 30 Agent PRs Introduced Real Vulnerabilities

title: LMDeploy CVE-2026-33626 — SSRF in LLM Inference Exploited 12h After Advisory (CVSS 7.5)
